independenceBoundary.rule: Fawn starts above stock Chromium through narrow CDP/Playwright adapters and does not require native runtime wins. The WGSL compiler and native WebGPU runtime can earn adoption independently; neither requires the other or Fawn. Doppler owns model semantics. Chromium hooks and browser-runtime integration are added only when measured benefits justify their compatibility and maintenance costs, and earn separate admission; prepared-program integration remains a separate treatment.
requiredEvidence: externally owned non-Doppler consumer of the selected compiler or runtime surface
independent semantic oracle, pinned inputs and reproducible installation
separately measured compiler or runtime advantage against the strongest eligible controls
voluntary maintainer adoption and retention across another release or workload
production signer authorization independent of the execution provider

surfaces.job: Provide independently usable WGSL analysis and target lowering. Evaluate compilation latency, diagnostics, supported shader semantics and generated-program performance separately from runtime execution.
surfaces.promotionGate: A concrete external compiler consumer verifies its declared outcome against independent controls and retains use without requiring DoeRuntime. New campaigns need explicit opportunity selection; closed browser transformations stay closed.

surfaces.job: Become Chromium's superior GPU execution foundation: own WebGPU validation, resources, submission, completion, memory, synchronization and selected browser GPU integration. Preserve independently useful native execution and compiler adoption.
surfaces.promotionGate: The gpuFoundation hierarchy requires unchanged application wins, full page WebGPU ownership, separately qualified wider GPU paths and explicit maintainability acceptance. A frozen non-Doppler application advantage remains necessary for independent runtime adoption; declared-program changes are disclosed, and external adoption and repeat retention remain independently evidenced.

surfaces.job: Record evidence of provider identity, correctness, fallback, replay, lifecycle, and release admissibility without requiring runtime replacement.
surfaces.promotionGate: Record incumbent and DoeRuntime evidence impartially with independent output validation, provider identity, explicit fallback, and replay; this feature does not itself prove runtime adoption.

surfaces.job: Provide durable browser workspaces where agents work, above Chromium: one shared service for durable authority, versioned observation, trusted action dispatch, recovery and reusable workflow adapters.
surfaces.promotionGate: A shared implemented service passes authority, uncertainty and workflow fault tests and demonstrates complete-task value against competent stock Chromium/Playwright. Documentation, artwork and GPU/browser receipts do not establish workspace acceptance.

surfaces.job: Test improvements offline: turn retained physical failures into minimized reproductions, candidate corrections, and permanent regression gates.
surfaces.promotionGate: A retained field failure produces a reusable qualified correction without weakening evidence or promotion rules.

gpuFoundation.objective: Doe becomes Chromium's superior GPU execution foundation.
gpuFoundation.workloadRole: Compute is one proving lane alongside graphics. Node, Bun, Doppler and ONNX supply workloads, integration surfaces and regressions; they do not define the product.
gpuFoundation.admissionRule: All hierarchy obligations must pass for the foundation claim. Collect maintainability evidence throughout integration. Freeze measurable bounds and version sequences before qualification; missing validators, bounds or bound receipts prevent admission. Existing roadmapProofs campaigns and their frozen contracts retain their verdicts and cannot alone establish this hierarchy.

hierarchy.outcome: Beat Dawn for unchanged WebGPU applications.
requiredEvidence: inference and general compute, a Three.js scene, an image/filter pipeline, particles or fluids, and texture upload through actual canvas presentation
p50/p95 advantage, preparation, CPU, GPU memory, independent correctness and no fallback under frozen workload contracts

hierarchy.outcome: Own real webpage WebGPU inside Chromium from device creation through destruction.
requiredEvidence: stock Chromium+Dawn versus forced-Doe Chromium from the same pinned source and build configuration except for the declared integration; ordinary applications unchanged
Doe-owned device and resource creation, shader compilation, submission, completion, readback, presentation and destruction; disabling Doe makes page operations fail
preserved lifecycle, process, sandbox and security behavior; no fallback and no workspace-treatment confounding

hierarchy.outcome: Expand into Chromium's wider GPU paths only after WebGPU application wins, page ownership, real-path tracing and measured integration selection.

separate source-bound ownership, correctness, compatibility and complete-operation benefit for each selected path; page WebGPU receipts do not transfer

hierarchy.outcome: Prove maintainability with evidence collected throughout integration; correctness and speed cannot substitute.
requiredEvidence: narrow Chromium patch series within predeclared scope and size bounds
independent reproducible clean builds and clean installation from pinned inputs, with artifact equivalence
successful Chromium-version rebases across a frozen sequence, including build, ownership, correctness, lifecycle and performance checks
measured reduction of duplicated backend responsibilities against a frozen source baseline, preserving behavior
clean/incremental build and development/qualification test cost within frozen absolute budgets and regression limits
reviewed readable ownership and diagnostics, with boundary-attributed fault reproductions

roadmapProofs.finalObjective: Removing Doe or Fawn and returning to Dawn or stock Chromium makes the product measurably worse. Usefulness beside Dawn and Chromium does not meet this bar.
roadmapProofs.currentStatement: Doe has promising execution evidence; Fawn has scoped workspace advantages. Neither has achieved the final objective.
roadmapProofs.selectionRule: These proofs select current technical work. Proof 1 includes immediate WebGPU application graphics alongside compute. Wider Chromium rendering is a separate later family, selected only after WebGPU application wins and measured integration opportunity; see docs/thesis.md#graphics-proof-families. Proof 3 selects the forced-Doe Chromium build for its frozen comparison only, not for adoption or wider rendering ownership. Correctness repairs, independent installation and technical release are not blocked.

proofs.outcome: Current Doe against Dawn on the initial qualification target: re-run the native and package rows on current code, audit suspicious wins, then run complete Doppler generation; also establish direct WebGPU application graphics wins under separately frozen workload contracts.
requiredEvidence: native and package rows re-run on current code on the initial qualification target
a fairness audit of every win at or above the suspicious-speedup ratio
complete Doppler generation correct against an independent reference
CPU and memory within frozen bounds
unchanged WebGPU graphics workloads: a complex Three.js scene, a 2D image/filter pipeline, particles or fluids, and texture upload through canvas presentation
graphics correctness, complete-frame p50/p95 advantage, preparation, CPU cost, GPU execution and GPU memory accounting, with submission, completion and presentation distinguished
separately frozen graphics campaign contracts and executable admission checks; page WebGPU provider ownership cannot establish wider Chromium rendering ownership

proofs.outcome: Current Metal confirmation: reproduce the strongest rows on current code, audit every result at or above the suspicious-speedup ratio, and fix or explain the ONNX Runtime tail regression.
requiredEvidence: the strongest Metal rows reproduced on current code and retained
a fairness audit of every result at or above the suspicious-speedup ratio
the ONNX Runtime tail regression fixed or explained by evidence
historical artifacts in ignored output are not admitted

proofs.outcome: Integrated Fawn and Doe against stock Chromium and Dawn: build the forced-Doe Chromium path, then run identical browser and agent workloads on every arm.
requiredEvidence: a forced-Doe Chromium build in which the page's WebGPU work is Doe-owned, with a disabled-Doe negative control
identical browser and agent workloads on every arm
the integrated system beats stock Chromium in task success, latency, memory, recovery and demanding GPU workloads
proofs.claimRule: Fawn earns the larger claim only when the complete integrated system beats stock Chromium on every required measure.

forbiddenInferences: DoeProof value does not imply DoeRuntime ownership.
Legacy Fawn shell build value does not imply DoeRuntime or Direct Protocol value.
DoeProof value and qualification cannot depend on Doppler availability or provider preference.
A component timing win does not imply an application win.
Node, native, Apple, AMD, browser, and Windows evidence never inherit promotion from one another.
DoeProof receipts, compiler breadth, internal benchmarks, and Doppler interoperability cannot substitute for DoeRuntime adoption.
Compiler adoption does not establish native runtime adoption, or conversely.
Verified elimination under a prospective application-replacement contract cannot relabel historical fixed-operation results.
Local isolated installation does not establish external operator reproduction or retained adoption.
Workspace policy validation does not establish implemented dispatch, durable ownership or safe action recovery.
Existing Chromium, GPU recovery, artwork or A/B/C/D receipts cannot establish Fawn workspace acceptance.
Fawn workspace value does not establish Chromium hook, DoeRuntime or Doppler model qualification.

reusableProgram.initialScope: Explicit fixed-shape buffer compute; source and shape changes invalidate affected state.
reusableProgram.demonstrationGate: Independent numerical parity, meaningful predeclared application outcome against persistent Dawn and wgpu, lifecycle and memory evidence, AMD Vulkan to Apple Metal reproduction, and transfer to another application.
reusableProgram.adoptionBoundary: Repository demonstrations do not establish external voluntary adoption or retention.

developmentEffectiveness.start: Timestamp of a retained reproducible problem with pinned source and inputs.
developmentEffectiveness.stop: Timestamp of independently verified improvement against frozen correctness and application acceptance.
developmentEffectiveness.recordingRule: Record elapsed time and evidence links in existing work records; retain unresolved and rejected attempts separately. No new measurement framework is required.
developmentEffectiveness.engineeringRule: Keep compiler, backends and host adapters independently testable. Reuse, refactoring and agent assistance serve the selected technical work; avoid abstractions that add execution overhead.
